title: Félix da Costa wins from pole as BMW take the top five
dek: António Félix da Costa took his first DTM victory from pole at Zandvoort by 0.473 seconds from Augusto Farfus, as BMW filled the top five and Jamie Green's championship lead shrank to five points.

chapters.title: A Saturday that belonged to BMW
text: Race 2 on Sunday 12 July followed a Saturday that had belonged to BMW. Marco Wittmann won Race 1 from second on the grid and the manufacturer took the first seven places for the first time in the series, with António Félix da Costa second on his first DTM podium. Jamie Green, the championship leader, ran into the gravel while sixth and scored nothing, but still led Mattias Ekström by 11 points, 81 to 70, with Pascal Wehrlein third on 68. Sunday's race was longer at 60 minutes plus one lap, with a mandatory pit stop, and it was run under cloud at about 18 degrees.

chapters.title: Félix da Costa takes his first pole
text: The morning qualifying session repeated Saturday's pattern. António Félix da Costa, who had never started a DTM race from pole position, lapped the 4.307-kilometre circuit in 1:30.483 for the first pole of his career, nearly eight tenths quicker than Farfus's pole time the day before. Bruno Spengler was second for MTEK, 0.058 seconds behind, with Augusto Farfus third on 1:30.623 and Wittmann fourth on 1:30.650. Each of BMW's four teams had one car in the top four, and Félix da Costa said afterwards that the lighter BMWs let the team get the tyres working at Zandvoort.

Miguel Molina was fifth in 1:30.674, the best of the Audis, and Wehrlein sixth in 1:30.809 as the leading Mercedes. Timo Glock was seventh, followed by Daniel Juncadella, Gary Paffett and Christian Vietoris, with Maxime Martin 11th, Edoardo Mortara 12th and Martin Tomczyk 13th. The championship contenders fared badly: Robert Wickens was 15th, Ekström 16th and Green 18th on 1:31.239, while Paul di Resta was 23rd and Lucas Auer, the Mercedes rookie, last of the 24 in 1:31.719.

chapters.title: A clean getaway at the front
text: Félix da Costa made a perfect start from pole and was clear of the field before the first corner. Spengler, who said he had struggled with his clutch all weekend, got away less well and had to defend hard against Farfus and Wittmann at the first corner, but he kept second place. Wehrlein also had a poor start and fell to ninth.

Behind the leaders the field soon got untidy. On the second lap Martin, third the day before, was hit by Tambay's Audi and dropped to the back of the field, where he would stay and finish 17th. Tambay faced no penalty for the contact.

chapters.title: Spengler loses second in the pits
text: The mandatory stops began at around the 20-minute mark. Glock was the first of the front-runners to stop, and the early stop lifted him from seventh to fourth. Spengler stopped before the leaders, but his crew had to hold him in the box for a moment to avoid an unsafe release, and when the leaders pitted Farfus came out ahead of him in second. Félix da Costa kept the lead through the stops.

Wittmann came out of the pits behind Lucas Auer, whose Mercedes had not yet stopped. Shortly afterwards Wittmann forced his way past and turned the Mercedes around in the process, and the Austrian went off the road.

chapters.title: Bonnet, airborne Mercedes and a drive-through
text: The disturbance in the pack after the stops led to a series of contacts. Tomczyk, who had gained five places at the start, was squeezed and pushed from behind in the bunch, touched Molina and lost the fastenings of his bonnet, which lifted and blocked his view. The BMW retired with damage.

On lap 21 Mortara and Juncadella touched at Turn 6. Juncadella, who said he had been pushed wide, hit a kerb, went airborne and landed hard, and he complained of back pain afterwards; neither car continued. Elsewhere Tom Blomqvist turned Wickens around at Tarzan, and Blomqvist was given a drive-through penalty. Blomqvist finished 18th, Wickens 19th.

chapters.title: Félix da Costa holds off Farfus
text: Félix da Costa won in 1:02:07.601 after 39 laps, his first DTM victory and one day after his first podium. Farfus stayed on his gearbox to the flag but never found a way past, finishing 0.473 seconds behind. Félix da Costa said he had kept his distance before Turn 1, because that was the only good place to pass. Spengler was third, 1.091 seconds behind, Glock fourth, 1.710, and Wittmann fifth after a hard race, 4.975 seconds from the winner. Glock also set the fastest lap, a 1:33.635 on lap 15.

Wehrlein recovered from his poor start to take sixth, 10.954 seconds back, as the best driver outside BMW. Ekström was seventh from 16th on the grid, ahead of Vietoris, Adrien Tambay and Paffett, who had run in the top ten early before a slow stop. Green was a quiet 13th, one place ahead of di Resta, a third race in a row without points for the championship leader, and his advantage had shrunk to five points.

chapters.title: BMW celebrate, the middle of the field complains
text: BMW Motorsport director Jens Marquardt called the weekend very positive and said it had all come together, but warned that the competition was much stronger than it looked and that the margins between the manufacturers were tiny from circuit to circuit. Félix da Costa said he was speechless after a fantastic weekend, with the pole and the win coming a day after his first podium. Schnitzer team principal Charly Lamm spoke of a great relief at standing on the top step, and said Félix da Costa had earned it.

Spengler said his car had been perfect but that the wait in the pit box for the safe release had cost him second place. Wittmann said he had lost out at the start behind his BMW colleagues and then had hard but fair duels with Molina; the contact with Auer damaged his car, he said, though his speed stayed good, and the gap to the front was too big to close. Martin called the second-lap contact an unfortunate situation in a hard-fought race and kept the memory of his Saturday podium. Tomczyk, who retired for a second race in a row, said he had been sandwiched in a bunch of cars and pushed from behind before the contact with Molina.

The racing in the midfield was the talk afterwards. Wickens called it a terrible race and said he had been touched by three Audi drivers within two laps. Juncadella said some drivers can only touch rather than race properly, and that this had happened with Mortara many times before. Former Mercedes motorsport chief Norbert Haug, working as a television expert, thought the pace was too rough and compared it to a pub brawl in which everyone joins once one person starts; he said the Mortara and Juncadella incident should be raised at the next drivers' briefing, and he questioned why Tambay had not been penalised.

In the championship Green still led on 81 points, but Wehrlein and Ekström were now level on 76, five behind. Mortara was fourth on 58, Wickens fifth on 57 and Spengler sixth on 52 after his podium. BMW had won both races of the weekend and filled all six podium places. The next round was the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, Austria, from 31 July to 2 August, the fifth of the nine race weekends.

facts.v: António Félix da Costa took the first pole position of his DTM career and converted it into his first DTM victory a day after his first podium.
